result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-day quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director usable wording plus metrics the team likely already tracks. A wins because it explicitly suggests retesting on new scenarios about a week and a month later, plus scoring real tickets in weeks 3–4. B never really covers checking what agents remember later. B is slightly stronger on stating the small-sample and confounding caveats, and its plan is a little tighter. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the numbers don't show on-the-job improvement, suggest suitable support metrics with time checkpoints, and give the director script with honest caveats. B is better because it adds a retest on new scenarios at about a week and a month, plus QA review of real tickets, which covers the retention item. A only tracks performance metrics at 30/60/90 days. A is slightly leaner, but B's six steps are still reasonable for a small team.
